name: Review (v2, on the crawl's building blocks)
description: (#2310 P4c/P4c-2, NOT the frozen `review` id) A code review built as a SECOND mission config on the crawl's shared blocks (#2301/#2310), never as a fork of it: `plan-<rule>` mints one `plan.sites` task per rule with `source: "diff"` (the DIFF-scoped strategy on the same plan_sites pattern `crawl.plan`'s tree walk uses — see plan_sites_step.rs); `unit-<rule>` GROWS one `crawl.unit` dispatch per planned site, `role_id: "reviewer"` (the SAME step kind crawl.json's `unit-<rule>` phase uses, generalized in this packet to read the Task's own role rather than a hardcoded `crawler`); `create-mods` reuses crawl's create-mod pattern (plus its own `gate-step`, #2310 P4c-2b) over this run's own findings; `deliver` (#2310 P4c-2b) gathers this run's own finding/mod stores and renders a GitHub review payload. Crawl never learns what a PR is (DESIGN.md): this document names no crawl MISSION-CONFIG id and `crawl.json` is untouched by this packet, but it does name two of crawl's STEP KINDS by their current ids — `crawl.unit` and `crawl.summary` — because that is where the shared blocks live today. The vocabulary is the leftover, not the coupling: P4d folds both into mission-agnostic kinds, and this document's step `kind` fields change with them.

inputs.name: workspace
inputs.description: Path to a workspace spec JSON naming the checked-out tree at the diff's own head — REQUIRED for every `plan-<rule>` step. Unlike the frozen `review` config's `worktree`/`github` inputs, a diff-scoped plan step reads through `workspace_spec::materialize`, the SAME mechanism `crawl.json` uses, so this run needs a real materialized source (a `path` source pointing at the checked-out tree is the common case — see the P4 brief's own live-plumbing-proof recipe, "over a tempdir tree of the post-diff fixture"). Must resolve to exactly ONE source.

inputs.name: diff_file
inputs.description: Path to the unified diff this review plans against. Canonicalized at step-config parse time.

inputs.name: intent_file
inputs.description: Path to the PR body / intent text `intent-vs-diff` compares the diff against. Mirrors the frozen `review` config's own input of the same name. READ, on every unit dispatch: each `unit-<rule>` task grows `"intent_file": "{{intent_file}}"` into its `crawl.unit` step's config, `UnitStepConfig::from_step` parses it (unit_step.rs L823-828, empty string filtered to absent so a launch that passes no `intent_file` is not a path-read failure), `run` reads the file (L1092) and `build_message` renders its text ahead of the window as "The stated intent for this change (a PR body or intent file) is:" (L342-345). Leave it unset and `intent-vs-diff` has nothing to compare the hunk against, so it reports nothing — the rule runs, sees no stated intent, and every unit it planned comes back empty.

inputs.name: head_sha
inputs.description: The diff's own head sha — mirrors the frozen `review` config's input. Reaches each `plan-<rule>` step's config but is not yet consumed (see `plan_sites_step.rs`'s module doc: `Plan.sources[0].sha` comes from the checked-out tree today, not this param).

inputs.name: github
inputs.description: owner/repo — mirrors the frozen `review` config's input. Reaches each `plan-<rule>` step's config but is not yet consumed (no fetch path exists yet — see `plan_sites_step.rs`'s module doc).

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Mirrors the frozen `review` config's input. Accepted for CLI-surface parity; not yet read by any step in this document.

inputs.name: bundler
inputs.description: Mirrors the frozen `review` config's input (the external-bundler plugin path). Accepted and IGNORED (#2310 P4c-2 item 4: declared "ignored" structurally, not detected by config id) — `review-v2` does not use the funnel's bundler; its planner reads `diff_file` directly. Passing it prints a named warning at launch time (before dispatch, on the `--dry-run` path too) saying it is ignored, so an operator carrying a `bundler=` param over from a `review` launch line gets a visible signal rather than a silent no-op.
inputs.ignored_reason: review-v2 does not use the funnel's bundler; its planner reads diff_file directly

inputs.name: envelope_out
inputs.description: Mirrors the frozen `review` config's input. Still NOT consumed (#2310 P4c-2b): `deliver.github_review` writes the rendered `{mode, review}` payload only (via `emit`), never a separate full envelope file — there is no envelope shape in this document's own pipeline for this to name.

inputs.name: emit
inputs.description: Path to write the rendered `{mode, review}` payload the `deliver` phase's `deliver-step` produces. `-` (or omitted) writes to stdout, matching the frozen `review` config's own `emit` contract.

inputs.name: attribution
inputs.description: Attribution text for the posted footer, threaded to the `deliver` phase's `deliver-step` — mirrors the frozen `review` config's own `attribution` input. Absent means no footer line (`deliver.github_review`'s own default), NOT the frozen config's envelope-derived default — this document has no member-record envelope to derive one from.

inputs.name: test_command
inputs.description: The gate command `create-mods` runs against a proposed mod before counting it confirmed (#2310 P4c — DESIGN.md "the changed files name the test targets"). Wired (#2310 P4c-2b): the `create-mod` task's `gate-step` (`mods.gate`) takes `{{item.tree_root}}` as its `workdir` and, for every mod naming the finding the task addresses, resolves the single source checkout beneath it, copies that checkout to a scratch dir, `git apply`s the mod's kit there, and only then runs this command INSIDE the patched copy (mods_gate.rs L193-202, L266-269, L305-306) — never in `tree_root` and never in the read-only source itself, so a gate can never mutate the tree a finding was observed in. `tree_root` is where the checkout is resolved FROM, not where the command runs. Each mod is recorded `gate_passed`/`gate_skipped_reason`. Leaving it unset means every mod is recorded `gate_skipped_reason: "no test_command configured"`, never gate-verified — and the visible consequence in the delivered review (#2310 fix loop A, S1-5) is that NO suggestion block is ever rendered: `deliver.github_review` turns a mod into a one-click suggestion only when its gate PASSED, so with no `test_command` every mod-form finding delivers as a "Worth a double check" thread instead.

inputs.name: rules
inputs.description: Comma-separated rule ids to review with, same selection mechanism as `crawl.json`'s own `rules` input — a `plan-<rule>` task whose rule is not named is pruned at mint with reason `not_selected`. Absent means every enabled plan task this document declares.

inputs.name: draws
inputs.description: How many times to dispatch each planned unit (#2310 P4c-2b — DESIGN.md "a draws-per-unit knob, off by default, ports the measured k-draw recall technique from the funnel"). Absent means 1 (`crawl.unit`'s own default) — one dispatch per unit, unchanged from before this input existed. `finding_refs` dedup on `(rule, file, line)` across a unit's own draws before `create-mods` grows from them, so a duplicate observation across draws never mints two coder tasks for the same window.

inputs.name: review-probe-high
inputs.description: Seat override for the `unit-<rule>` tasks — same param name shape the P4 brief's live-plumbing-proof recipe uses (`--param review-probe-high=probe-4b`), kept even though this document has no probe/judge/verify staffing split of its own YET: a single seat resolves every `unit-<rule>` task via the `reviewer` role's own `role_profiles.reviewer` binding, or this override.

inputs.name: dry_run
inputs.description: The generic `mission launch --dry-run` flag, injected by the CLI layer. Prints the task/step graph this launch would mint and mints nothing.

phases.description: One planning task per rule, diff-scoped. Each materializes `workspace`, reads `diff_file`, and writes plan/<rule>.json — the SAME `Plan` content shape `crawl.plan` writes (`plan.sites`'s tree-source path IS `crawl.plan`'s own `plan_one_rule`), just produced from a diff's hunks instead of a tree walk.

tasks.description: Plan the `intent-vs-diff` rule over the diff.
Plan the `existing-solution` rule over the diff.
Plan the `shared-symbol-callers` rule over the diff.
Plan the `union-vs-enum` rule over the diff.
Plan the `test-gap` rule over the diff.
Plan the crawl's `swallowed-error` rule over the diff — reused via its `scope: ["tree","diff"]`.
Plan the crawl's `unnamed-predicate` rule over the diff — reused via its `scope: ["tree","diff"]`.

phases.description: One dispatch per planned unit, `role_id: "reviewer"` — the SAME `crawl.unit` kind `crawl.json`'s own `crawl` phase uses, dispatching a different role because #2310 P4c made the role a Task property the kind reads rather than a hardcoded `"crawler"`.
This run's totals, read back through every `crawl.unit` step's own outcome — the SAME `crawl.summary` kind `crawl.json` uses.

tasks.description: Total this review's units, findings and tokens.

phases.description: Reuses crawl's create-mods `create-mod-step` verbatim (DESIGN.md "Review reuses the create-mods phase") — that step's shape is byte-identical to `crawl.json`'s own. `crawl.json`'s create-mods never runs tests (findings are proposals over a read-only tree, no test target implied); a review's mod SHOULD run the changed files' own test target before it counts as confirmed (DESIGN.md "the changed files name the test targets, which is what makes confirmation cheap enough to do per finding") — this task's shape diverges from crawl's in exactly THREE places, all of them the gate: (1) a second step, `gate-step` (`mods.gate`, #2310 P4c-2b), where crawl's task has only `create-mod-step`; (2) `grow.config.for_key: "{{item.key}}"`, which is how the gate step knows WHICH finding's mods to gate; (3) `grow.config.test_command: "{{test_command}}"`, the command itself. Everything else — `workdir`, `brief_refs`, the coder's message — is byte-identical to `crawl.json`'s own. The gate step does NOT run `test_command` in `{{item.tree_root}}`: it takes that path as its `workdir`, resolves the single source checkout under it, copies that checkout to a scratch dir, `git apply`s the mod's kit there, and runs the command inside the PATCHED copy (mods_gate.rs L193-202, L305-306), recording `gate_passed`/`gate_skipped_reason` on every mod naming this task's finding. One more difference is a matter of default rather than shape: `crawl.json`'s own `create-mod` task carries `"enabled": false` and is pruned at mint, while this one carries no `enabled` field at all and therefore runs.

tasks.display_name: Create mod: propose the change one finding describes
tasks.description: Dispatch one `coder` per finding — one task per entry in the summary's `finding_refs`.

config.message:
A finding recorded earlier in this run is appended below. Your job is to PROPOSE the change that finding describes, as a mod. The workspace you have been given is the tree the finding was observed in, mounted read-only: you cannot edit it, and you are not meant to.

1. Read the file the finding names, around the line it names.
2. If the finding does not hold against what you read, record nothing and say why.
3. Otherwise write the smallest change that resolves it as a unified diff against the file as it is, and call `create_mod` with: `kit` = one sentence saying what to apply and the exact diff; `for` = the finding's key exactly as the block below spells it.

Do not run tests, and do not touch anything the finding does not name. The mod is your product; someone else integrates it.

phases.description: #2310 P4c-2b closes the gap the `create-mods` phase's own description names: `records.gather` reads THIS mission's own finding/mod stores (scoped by mission id — the way `finding list --mission`/`mod list --mission` resolve it) plus `diff_file`, into the typed shape `deliver.github_review` renders. Two steps of ONE task, `records-gather-step` then `deliver-step` — the SAME same-task-predecessor `Step.output` -> `input` wiring (`scheduler::gather_inputs`) every other multi-step task in this codebase uses, never a new mechanism. `run_on: ["complete","error"]` on the task documents the intent DESIGN.md's own retirement finding names ("an errored run rendered nothing... None were in a step") — an errored `create-mods` phase must not silence delivery; this task declares no `depends_on` at all (an edge naming `create-mod`, a grow TEMPLATE, is refused at validation — see `mission_config::interpret`'s own doc), so ordering comes from `create-mods` being an earlier PHASE in this document, the same phase-ordering `crawl.json`'s `summarize` phase relies on to see every grown `crawl.unit`'s results with no `depends_on` of its own.

tasks.display_name: Deliver: gather this run's records and render a GitHub review
tasks.description: Gather then deliver — see this phase's own description.
